questions.question_text: Which expression writes $\underset{\sim}{a}=\begin{pmatrix}-8\\3\end{pmatrix}$ as the sum of its component vectors?

options.why: Reversed the sign of each component.
Read the column vector bottom-to-top, so the components are swapped.
Swapped the components and reversed both signs.

questions.question_text: A vector has magnitude $16$ and an angle of inclination of $120^{\circ}$. Write it in exact component form.

options.why: Used the reference angle $60^{\circ}$ and lost the negative sign of $\cos 120^{\circ}$.
Swapped the sine and cosine, so $r\sin\theta$ was used for the horizontal component.
Swapped the sine and cosine and also lost the negative sign.

questions.question_text: A vector has magnitude $25$ and an angle of inclination of $310^{\circ}$. Write it in component form, with each component correct to one decimal place.

options.why: Used the reference angle $50^{\circ}$ and lost the negative sign of $\sin 310^{\circ}$.
Swapped the sine and cosine between the two components.
Swapped the sine and cosine and also lost the negative sign.

questions.question_text: A current flows at $60$ m/s on a true bearing of $300^{\circ}$. Resolve it into exact east and north components, written as $\underset{\sim}{i}$ (east) and $\underset{\sim}{j}$ (north) components.

options.why: Used cosine for the east component and sine for the north component, measuring the bearing from east instead of north.
Used the reference angle $60^{\circ}$ and lost both signs, giving the opposite direction.
Swapped sine and cosine and also lost both signs.
Read the vertical step as the horizontal one, swapping the two components.
Read the lengths of the steps but ignored that both are in negative directions.
Swapped the two components and also ignored the negative directions.

questions.solution_text:
The arrow runs $5$ units left and $4$ units down.
$\underset{\sim}{v}=-5\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}$

questions.question_text: A force of $90$ N acts at $65^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. Find its horizontal component, correct to one decimal place.

options.why: Used $90\sin 65^{\circ}$, which gives the vertical component instead of the horizontal one.
Divided by $\cos 65^{\circ}$ instead of multiplying by it.
Evaluated $\cos 65^{\circ}$ but forgot to multiply by the $90$ N magnitude.

questions.question_text: A $70$ km/h wind blows on a true bearing between $000^{\circ}$ and $090^{\circ}$, and its east component is $35$ km/h. Find the bearing.

options.why: Used $70\cos\beta=35$, taking cosine for the east component instead of sine.
Gave the second solution of $\sin\beta=0.5$, which lies outside the stated range $000^{\circ}$ to $090^{\circ}$.
Used cosine instead of sine and then took the solution outside the stated range.

questions.question_text: A vector has magnitude $34$ and an angle of inclination $\theta$ in the second quadrant with $\sin\theta=\frac{8}{17}$. Write the vector in component form.

options.why: Took $\cos\theta=\frac{15}{17}$ as positive, ignoring that $\theta$ is in the second quadrant.
Swapped $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ between the two components.
Swapped $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ and put the negative sign on the wrong component.

questions.solution_text:
$\sin\theta=\frac{8}{17}$, so the right-angled triangle has sides $8$, $15$ and $17$.
Since $\theta$ is in the second quadrant, $\cos\theta=-\frac{15}{17}$.
$x=34\times\left(-\frac{15}{17}\right)$
$=-30$
$y=34\times\frac{8}{17}$
$=16$
The vector is $-30\underset{\sim}{i}+16\underset{\sim}{j}$.
